keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Lusitanian row; the pages have no infobox area. The gazetteer's 'Lusitania' region (all Portugal south of the Douro districts, Badajoz, Caceres and Salamanca) overshoots, taking the Alentejo and the Algarve south of the Tagus, so the region is drawn from the districts between the Douro and the Tagus plus Caceres. The eastern border 'passed through Salmantica and Caesarobriga' (Salamanca is not drawn). Soft edges.

ledger.note: 155-139 BC: the Lusitanian War ('155 to 139 BC'). Galba's massacre of the surrendering divisions (152 context); 'The Lusitanians chose Viriathus as their leader' (148); Tribola (148); Venus mountain (143); Caepio's complaint about the treaty, then war. The Lusitanians page says 'Starting in 193 BCE, the Lusitanians fought the Romans', but the pages give no ground taken or held before 155 (raids, praetors' campaigns), so the contest is drawn from 155; Galba defeated them in 150, Viriathus was their leader from 147/148.

ledger.note: 139 BC: Viriathus 'was found dead in the morning', murdered under Caepio's command; the Lusitanians 'became Roman subjects' and 'a period of relative peace' followed; a revolt in 80-72 under Sertorius.

notes: New state. Lusitania from a 500 placeholder to Viriathus' death (139). identity.wikipedia points at the war page, the only one opened; the 'Lusitanians' page itself was not fetched. Wikidata unverified. Revised 2026-10-19 after review: every Lusitania region (found, contest, loss, dissolve, successor, war zone) is now the Portuguese districts between the Douro and the Tagus plus Caceres, not the gazetteer's 'Lusitania' (which takes in the Alentejo and the Algarve south of the Tagus, and Badajoz and Salamanca); the Lusitanians page was reopened: the fighting 'starting in 193 BCE' gives no ground taken or held, so the contest still starts in 155 (noted on the event); keyframes added; capitals stay empty (no page names a Lusitanian town).
